cards.question: How long does a TFS freeze applied by Lumara last?
options: For 30 days unless the Attorney General extends it
Until the person is delisted or the EOCN communicates a cancellation
For 10 working days, as with an FIU suspension
Until the customer provides evidence of legitimate funds
cards.explanation: EOCN guidance states that TFS freezes have no time limit. They end on delisting or an EOCN freezing cancellation communicated through goAML. The 10-day and 30-day periods belong to the FIU's separate powers under Article 5 of the decree-law.

cards.title: Common TFS mistakes
cards.body:
- Screening only **new** customers after a list update instead of the whole book.
- Forgetting **beneficial owners, authorised signatories and attorneys**.
- Using a CNMR for a **foreign unilateral list** match: those lists need supervisor guidance and possibly an STR.
- Lifting a partial-match suspension before the **EOCN** responds.
- Warning the customer before the freeze. Staff must not tip off.

Breaching EOCN TFS instructions is a crime with a fine of at least AED 20,000 and/or prison (Article 33), on top of supervisory penalties.

items.label: Freeze without delay
items.detail: The outer limit after a designation, per EOCN guidance.

items.label: CNMR or PNMR deadline
items.detail: Five business days from freezing, suspending or rejecting.

items.label: ID chase for prospects
items.detail: Ten business days to resolve a partial match before rejecting.

items.label: Ownership test
items.detail: Entities majority-owned by a designated person are frozen too.

cards.title: Stage 4 take-aways
items: UAE TFS covers the UAE Local Terrorist List and the UN Consolidated List under Cabinet Resolution 74 of 2020.
Register for EOCN alerts, screen on every update, freeze confirmed matches within 24 hours and without notice.
File a CNMR or PNMR through goAML within five business days; document false positives.
Freeze entities more than 50% owned or controlled by designated persons and anyone acting for them.
PF and sanctions evasion often involve no listed names: watch trade red flags and report suspicion to the FIU.

cards.prompt: Which systems, files or people in your area would a list update need to reach within the hour? Where could a designated name hide: a signatory, an owner, a counterparty or an old closed account?

quiz.question: Which lists does UAE targeted financial sanctions implementation cover under Cabinet Resolution 74 of 2020?
options: The UAE Local Terrorist List and the UN Consolidated List
Only the UN Security Council Consolidated List, as adopted by Cabinet decision
The UAE list plus all foreign unilateral lists
Only lists published by the CBUAE
quiz.explanation: EOCN guidance defines the Sanctions Lists as the UAE Local Terrorist List issued by the Cabinet and the UNSC Consolidated List. Foreign unilateral lists are handled differently.

quiz.question: How does EOCN guidance define freezing 'without delay'?
options: Within five business days of the designation being published by the EOCN
Immediately, or within 24 hours of designation
Within ten business days after obtaining ID
By the end of the following calendar month
quiz.explanation: The guidance defines without delay as immediately or within 24 hours of a designation. Five business days is the reporting deadline for CNMRs and PNMRs.

quiz.question: How does Lumara receive automated updates on UAE and UN sanctions designations?
options: Through monthly CBUAE circulars sent to every licensed bank's compliance officer
By waiting for the FIU to call
By registering with the EOCN Notification Alert System
Through the customer's annual KYC review
quiz.explanation: Registration with the EOCN Notification Alert System is the first of the four TFS steps. It sends automatic notifications of designations, delistings and amendments.

quiz.question: Screening finds a customer whose name and date of birth match a UN-listed person, but whose nationality differs, and the ID on file does not resolve it. What should Lumara do?
options: Freeze permanently and file a CNMR, because the date of birth matches exactly
Suspend and file a PNMR within five business days
Treat it as a false positive and continue
Close the account and tell the customer why
quiz.explanation: This is a partial name match on an existing customer. EOCN guidance requires suspension without delay, a PNMR through goAML within five business days and keeping the suspension until the EOCN instructs.

quiz.question: A prospect's name partially matches a listed person and the prospect does not provide ID documents within 10 business days. What next?
options: Open the account and keep chasing the ID documents for another month
Reject it and file a PNMR within five business days
File a CNMR because the prospect refused
Do nothing, because prospects are not customers
quiz.explanation: For potential customers, the guidance allows a reasonable time, 10 business days, to obtain ID. If the match cannot be resolved, the transaction is rejected and a PNMR filed within five business days.

quiz.question: A designated person owns 51% of a company that banks with Lumara. The other owners are not designated. What applies?
options: Freeze only 51% of the company's balance
Freeze the other owners' personal accounts too
No action, because the company itself is not listed
Freeze the company's funds without delay
quiz.explanation: EOCN guidance treats an entity more than 50% owned by a designated person as subject to freezing. The other owners' own funds are not frozen unless they act for the designated person.

quiz.question: A customer matches a name only on a foreign unilateral sanctions list, not on the UAE or UN lists. What does EOCN guidance advise?
options: File a CNMR through goAML within five business days of identifying the match
Freeze immediately under Resolution 74 of 2020
Consult the supervisor and consider an STR
Ignore it, because only UAE law matters
quiz.explanation: CNMRs and PNMRs are only for matches with the UAE Local Terrorist List and UN list. For other lists, the guidance says to consult the supervisory authority and consider an STR to the FIU.

quiz.question: Which is a proliferation financing red flag listed in EOCN guidance?
options: A company paying staff salaries through a payroll provider
A retail customer opening a savings account
Payment by a party that is not the consignee, with no clear reason
An exporter using a well-known shipping line on a direct, regular route to its usual buyer
quiz.explanation: EOCN guidance lists payment by an entity other than the consignee without clear economic reason, among other trade and maritime indicators such as circuitous routes and licence mismatches.

quiz.question: Which instrument contains the UAE Control List of strategic and dual-use goods?
options: Cabinet Resolution No. 134 of 2025
Federal Decree-Law No. 10 of 2025
Cabinet Resolution No. 50 of 2020
Cabinet Resolution No. 74 of 2020
quiz.explanation: EOCN's CPF guidance explains that Cabinet Resolution No. 50 of 2020 contains the UAE Control List. Resolution 74 of 2020 is the TFS framework and Resolution 134 the AML executive regulations.

quiz.question: Under Article 33 of the 2025 decree-law, what is the minimum fine for violating EOCN instructions on targeted financial sanctions, if a fine is imposed?
quiz.explanation: Article 33 punishes violations of TFS instructions with imprisonment and a fine of not less than AED 20,000, or either penalty, in addition to supervisory penalties under Article 17.

sessions.title: The Institution's Programme: People, Governance and Penalties
sessions.summary: Bring it together for the CBUAE inspection: internal policies approved by senior management, the compliance officer's duties, role-based training, independent audit, new products and group controls, and the administrative and criminal penalties for failure.
objectives: List the minimum contents of internal AML/CFT/CPF policies under Article 21 of Resolution 134
Describe the compliance officer's status and duties under Article 22
Plan role-based AML/CFT/CPF training that meets the regulations and EOCN expectations
Explain senior management accountability and the CBUAE's administrative penalties

cards.title: The inspection letter
cards.setting: Executive floor, Lumara head office, Abu Dhabi. 4:00 pm.

lines.text: The CBUAE inspection starts in three weeks. Maryam, tell me plainly: what will they ask me and the board?
Whether our risk assessment is current, whether senior management approved our policies, and whether controls actually work.
Last year's audit flagged slow alert reviews. We postponed the monitoring upgrade to save costs.
They'll ask about that too. And they'll test whether staff training is real, role-based and documented.
Can I personally be held responsible if something slips through?
Let's answer that properly. This is the Boardroom, the last stage before the final exam.

cards.title: Six building blocks of the programme

scenes.heading: Policies approved at the top
scenes.narration: Article 21 requires internal policies, controls and procedures approved by senior management, proportionate to the bank's risks, size and activities, and kept up to date.

scenes.heading: A compliance officer with clout
scenes.narration: The bank must appoint a compliance officer at management level, with independence in decision-making and the right competence and experience.

scenes.heading: Fit staff, trained staff
scenes.narration: Policies must include screening so employees meet high standards of fitness and propriety, and periodic programmes and workshops to build staff capacity.

scenes.heading: Independent audit
scenes.narration: An independent audit function must test whether AML/CFT/CPF policies, controls and procedures are effective and adequate.

scenes.heading: Beyond head office
scenes.narration: Policies apply across branches and majority-owned subsidiaries, with group-wide information sharing under confidentiality safeguards.

cards.title: Who owns what at Lumara
cards.caption: Responsibility sits at every level, but approval and resourcing start at the top.

items.label: Board and senior management
items.detail: Approve policies, set risk appetite, resource the programme, act on reports.

items.label: Compliance officer
items.detail: Management-level, independent: monitoring, STR decisions, reviews, training plans.

items.label: Business and operations
items.detail: Apply CDD, screening and escalation every day.

items.label: Independent audit
items.detail: Tests effectiveness and reports findings for remediation.

cards.title: The compliance officer's duties (Article 22)
cards.prompt: Match each duty to what it looks like in practice at Lumara.

pairs.right: Overseeing transactions and alerts linked to possible ML, TF or PF
Reviewing internal reports and deciding, with reasons, whether to notify the FIU
Assessing AML/CFT/CPF systems against the law and reporting to senior management
Developing, delivering and documenting ongoing employee training plans
Giving the CBUAE and the FIU the data and record access they request

cards.question: Under Article 22 of Resolution 134, how must the compliance officer be positioned?
options: Within the internal audit department so findings stay independent
As an external consultant to avoid conflicts of interest
Reporting to the head of retail so issues reach the business quickly
At management level, with independence in decision-making and suitable competence
cards.explanation: Article 22 requires a compliance officer appointed at management level, under the institution's responsibility, with independence in decisions and appropriate competence and experience. Audit must remain a separate, independent function.

cards.title: Training that meets the rules
cards.body:
The training duty has several sources:

- **Article 21(5)** of Resolution 134: periodic programmes and workshops to build the capacity of compliance staff and other relevant employees.
- **Article 22(4)**: the compliance officer develops, implements and **documents** ongoing training plans for employees on ML, TF and PF and how to combat them.
- **EOCN TFS guidance**: ongoing TFS training and awareness for relevant employees **and senior management**.
- **EOCN CPF guidance**: PF basics for all staff, with extra PF typology training for compliance, audit and trade finance.

CBUAE best-practice guidance adds induction for new joiners, regular refreshers, role-based modules, needs assessments and testing. Follow your bank's training policy for the exact frequency.

cards.title: Everyone, or role-based?
cards.prompt: Decide whether each topic belongs in Lumara's all-staff module or in a role-based module.

items.text: What ML, TF and PF are and why they matter in the UAE
How to raise an internal report and avoid tipping off
Basic principles of proliferation and its financing
Dual-use goods and trade document red flags
Resolving partial name matches and filing PNMRs
Board oversight of the enterprise risk assessment
Applying the beneficial ownership cascade to complex structures

lines.text: So, personally. What's my exposure?
Two routes. The CBUAE can restrict the powers of, suspend or seek the replacement of directors and managers found responsible for violations.
And under the criminal provisions, a manager can be punished if a crime happened because they breached the duties of their position and knew of it.
Then postponing the monitoring upgrade wasn't just a budget decision.
Exactly. Approving, resourcing and following up the programme is how senior management shows it took its duties seriously.

cards.back: The lightest measure, recorded against the institution.
From AED 10,000 to AED 5 million for each violation, with higher fines possible for repeats within a year.
Prohibiting the violator from working in the relevant sector for a set period.
Limiting the powers of board members or managers responsible, including appointing a temporary supervisor.
Suspending responsible directors or managers, or requiring their replacement.
Suspending or restricting the activity, or revoking the licence. Penalties may also be published.

cards.title: The board decision
cards.situation: At the board risk committee, the chief financial officer proposes deferring the transaction monitoring upgrade for another year and cutting role-based training to a single online module, to protect profit. The audit report flagged slow alert reviews, and the CBUAE inspection is three weeks away.

choices.text: Approve the deferral and cuts; the inspection will focus on policies, not systems
choices.outcome: Risky and wrong. Supervisors test whether controls work, and penalties can reach responsible managers. Ignoring audit findings undermines the whole programme.

choices.text: Reject the cuts, approve a resourced remediation plan with owners and dates, and ask the compliance officer to report progress directly to the committee
choices.outcome: Best answer. Senior management approves and resources the programme, acts on independent audit findings and receives the compliance officer's periodic reports.

choices.text: Approve the deferral but ask compliance to write a stronger policy document instead
choices.outcome: Paper does not fix slow alert reviews. The regulations require policies to be applied, monitored and enhanced where necessary.

choices.text: Move the compliance officer under the CFO to align costs and controls
choices.outcome: This would weaken the compliance officer's independence, which Article 22 requires.

cards.title: Getting inspection-ready
cards.prompt: Put Lumara's preparation steps in a sensible order.
steps: Refresh the enterprise risk assessment against the National Risk Assessment
Update policies to the 2025 law and regulations and obtain senior management approval
Close or plan remediation for open audit findings with owners and dates
Confirm role-based training was delivered, tested and documented
Compliance officer reports results and gaps to senior management
Assemble evidence for the CBUAE: risk assessment, policies, MI, STR and TFS records

cards.question: What is the purpose of the independent audit function required by Article 21?
options: To test whether the AML/CFT/CPF policies, controls and procedures are effective and adequate
To file STRs when the compliance officer is unavailable
To approve new customers rated high risk
To replace the compliance officer's periodic reports to senior management
cards.explanation: Article 21(6) requires an independent audit function to test the effectiveness and adequacy of internal policies, controls and procedures. It does not take over the compliance officer's reporting or approval roles.

cards.title: Two duties people forget
cards.body:
- **New products and technology (Article 24):** assess ML, TF and PF risk **before** launching a new product, practice, delivery channel or technology, and put controls in place first.
- **Group and foreign operations (Articles 32-33):** run group-wide programmes for branches and majority-owned subsidiaries, share information with confidentiality and anti-tipping-off safeguards, and apply UAE-level measures abroad where local rules are weaker. If the host country prevents that, take extra measures and inform the CBUAE.

cards.title: Worked example: Lumara's compliance officer report
cards.body:
Maryam's periodic report to senior management, which the CBUAE can request a copy of, covers:

- **Risk:** changes to the enterprise risk assessment and the National Risk Assessment inputs.
- **Reporting:** internal reports received, STRs filed, average decision time and reasons for not filing.
- **TFS:** list updates handled, freezes, CNMRs and PNMRs filed, and screening coverage tests.
- **Training:** completion and test results by role, including board sessions.
- **Audit and remediation:** open findings, owners, dates and status.
- **Decisions needed:** resources and approvals required from senior management.

The report records management's observations and decisions, which shows the supervisor that oversight is real.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways: what the CBUAE expects
items: Policies approved by senior management, proportionate to risk and kept current with the 2025 texts.
A management-level, independent compliance officer who decides on STRs, reviews systems, reports and runs documented training.
Fit-and-proper staff screening, role-based training for staff and senior management, and an independent audit function.
Assess new products before launch and run group-wide controls across branches and subsidiaries.
The CBUAE can fine up to AED 5 million per violation and act against responsible managers; managers can also face criminal liability.

cards.prompt: If a CBUAE inspector asked you tomorrow to show how you apply one AML/CFT/CPF control in your job, what evidence could you point to, and what is missing?

quiz.question: Who must approve Lumara's internal AML/CFT/CPF policies, controls and procedures under Article 21?
options: The CBUAE before every update
The UAE FIU
Senior management
Each branch manager for their branch
quiz.explanation: Article 21 of Resolution 134 requires internal policies, controls and procedures approved by senior management, proportionate to risks and size and reviewed on an ongoing basis.

quiz.question: Which item is among the minimum contents of internal policies listed in Article 21?
options: A guaranteed annual bonus for every member of the compliance department
Fit-and-proper screening when appointing employees
Annual customer satisfaction surveys
A ban on all cash transactions
quiz.explanation: Article 21 lists CDD measures, STR procedures, compliance arrangements with a management-level compliance officer, employee fit-and-proper screening, periodic capacity-building programmes and independent audit.

quiz.question: Which duty does Article 22(4) give the compliance officer?
options: Approving the bank's annual budget and capital plan before submission to the board
Prosecuting money laundering offences
Issuing licences to new branches
Developing and documenting ongoing employee training plans
quiz.explanation: Article 22(4) makes the compliance officer responsible for developing, implementing and documenting ongoing programmes and training plans for employees on the crimes and how to combat them.

quiz.question: To whom does the compliance officer submit periodic reports on the bank's AML/CFT/CPF systems under Article 22?
options: Directly to senior management; a copy to the supervisor on request
Only to the internal audit department, which then decides what to escalate
Only to the UAE FIU
To the customer service team for awareness
quiz.explanation: Article 22(3) requires periodic reports submitted directly to senior management, including their observations and decisions, with a copy sent to the supervisory authority on request.

quiz.question: According to EOCN TFS guidance, who should receive ongoing TFS training and awareness sessions?
options: Only the screening team
Relevant employees and senior management
Only new joiners in their first month
Only staff in branches near borders
quiz.explanation: EOCN guidance requires reporting entities to conduct ongoing TFS training and awareness sessions for relevant employees and senior management.

quiz.question: What range of administrative fines per violation can the CBUAE impose under Article 17 of the 2025 decree-law?
options: AED 10,000 to AED 5 million
AED 1,000 to AED 100,000
AED 50,000 to AED 1 million
AED 5 million to AED 100 million
quiz.explanation: Article 17(1)(b) sets administrative fines of not less than AED 10,000 and not more than AED 5 million for each violation. AED 5 million to 100 million is the criminal fine range for legal persons.

quiz.question: A bank repeats the same violation within a year of being fined for it. What does Article 17 allow the supervisor to do?
options: Nothing, because the matter is closed
Impose an incremental administrative fine
Only issue a private warning
Transfer the case to the EOCN
quiz.explanation: Article 17(3) allows an incremental administrative fine when the same violation recurs within a period not exceeding one year from the previous fine.

quiz.question: Lumara plans to launch a new app-based account opening channel next month. What does Article 24 require first?
options: Launch first and assess the risks within a year, once real usage data is available
Assess the risks and set controls before launch
Obtain approval from the UAE FIU
Limit the app to UAE nationals
quiz.explanation: Article 24 requires institutions to identify and assess risks from new products, practices, delivery mechanisms and technologies before launch or use, and to take measures to manage and mitigate them.

quiz.question: A chief executive knew of weaknesses that led to a laundering offence through his bank and ignored the duties of his position. What can follow under Article 27(5)?
options: Only a fine on the bank, because the bank benefited from the transactions
Nothing, because only the bank is liable
A warning letter to the board
Personal imprisonment and/or a fine
quiz.explanation: Article 27(5) allows punishment of the person responsible for actual management of a legal person by imprisonment and/or fine when they were aware and the crime resulted from their breach of the duties of their position.

quiz.question: A foreign subsidiary of Lumara operates where local AML rules are weaker and the host law blocks some UAE-level measures. What must Lumara do?
options: Take extra measures and notify the CBUAE
Apply only the host country's weaker rules, because local law always prevails abroad
Close the subsidiary immediately
Stop sharing any information with the subsidiary
quiz.explanation: Article 33 requires majority-owned foreign branches and subsidiaries to apply UAE-consistent measures where permitted; if the host country prevents this, the institution takes additional measures and informs the supervisor.

regulators: Executive Office for Control and Non-Proliferation (EOCN)

references.title: Federal Decree by Law No. (10) of 2025 Regarding Anti-Money Laundering, and Combating the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation Financing
references.note: Sets the ML, TF and PF offences, FIU suspension and freezing powers, supervisory penalties, the duty to report suspicion through the FIU's electronic system, preventive duties of financial institutions, tipping-off and TFS offences and good-faith protection for reporters.

references.title: Cabinet Resolution No. (134) of 2025 Regarding the Executive Regulations of Federal Decree by Law No. (10) of 2025
references.note: Risk assessment, CDD triggers and thresholds, beneficial ownership, PEPs, suspicious transaction reporting and tipping off, internal policies including training, compliance officer duties, record keeping, correspondent banking and wire transfers.

references.title: Cabinet Resolution No. (74) of 2020 Regarding the UAE List of Terrorists and Implementation of UN Security Council Resolutions
references.note: Requires financial institutions to register for list notifications, screen, freeze without delay and without prior notice, notify the supervisor and not tip off.

references.title: Guidance on Targeted Financial Sanctions
references.issuer: Executive Office for Control and Non-Proliferation (EOCN)
references.note: Registration in the Notification Alert System, screening triggers, freezing within 24 hours, CNMR and PNMR filing through goAML within five business days, ownership and control rules, other sanctions regimes and staff training.

references.title: Guidance on Counter Proliferation Financing for FIs, DNFBPs, and VASPs
references.issuer: Executive Office for Control and Non-Proliferation (EOCN)
references.provision: Sections on dual-use goods, staff training and red flags
references.note: Explains the UAE Control List and EOCN licensing of dual-use goods, PF and sanctions-evasion red flags for trade and maritime business, and expects PF training for all staff with more for higher-risk roles.

references.title: Guidance for Licensed Financial Institutions on Suspicious Transaction Reporting
references.note: Explains when and how to file STRs and SARs with the UAE FIU, the compliance officer's role and staff escalation.

references.title: Guidance for Licensed Financial Institutions on Customer Due Diligence/Know Your Customer and Record-Keeping
references.note: Sets expectations for identification and verification, beneficial ownership, risk-based EDD and SDD, ongoing monitoring and record retention.

references.title: Guidance for Licensed Financial Institutions on the Risks Relating to Politically Exposed Persons
references.note: Expects identification of PEPs, family members and close associates, risk rating, senior approval and ongoing monitoring rather than blanket refusal.

references.title: Guidance for Licensed Financial Institutions on Risks Related to Proliferation Finance
references.note: Explains PF risk, sanctions evasion typologies and enhanced measures for licensed financial institutions.

references.title: Guidance for Licensed Financial Institutions on Correspondent Banking and Expectations for Managing Correspondent Banking Relationships
references.note: Treats correspondent relationships as higher risk and describes respondent due diligence, nested relationship controls and screening.

references.title: Best Practices for Licensed Financial Institutions on Implementing Role-Based AML/CFT/CPF Training
references.note: Supervisory best practice on induction, refresher and role-based training, training needs assessment, testing and records.

references.title: Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism and Illegal Organisations Guidelines for Financial Institutions
references.note: Guidance expecting staff screening and training tailored to customer-facing staff, compliance staff, senior management and the board.

bank.question: A Lumara procedure still cites articles of Cabinet Decision No. 10 of 2019. What is the best assessment?
options: It must be updated, because Resolution 134 of 2025 repealed that decision
It is fine, because the 2019 decision still runs alongside the new one
It must be updated only if the CBUAE requests it
It is fine, because procedures do not need legal references
bank.explanation: Resolution 134 of 2025 expressly repealed Cabinet Decision No. 10 of 2019. Earlier regulations survive only where they do not conflict until replaced, and the executive regulations have now been replaced, so procedures should map to the new articles.

bank.question: A customer's funds came from a lawful salary, and he sends them to pay for a friend to travel abroad to train with a terrorist group. Which statement is right?
options: It is not an offence, because the funds were earned lawfully and taxed
It is money laundering because funds crossed a border
This can be terrorist financing, though the money is clean
It is an offence only if the friend commits an attack
bank.explanation: Article 3 covers funds from any source and specifically includes financing travel for the purpose of terrorist acts or training. Actual use in an attack is not required.

bank.question: Which pairing of authority and function is correct for a UAE onshore bank?
options: EOCN analyses STRs; the FIU maintains and publishes the sanctions lists
CBUAE: STR analysis; EOCN: bank licensing
FIU: bank inspections; CBUAE: list notifications
CBUAE supervises and penalises; the FIU analyses STRs
bank.explanation: The CBUAE supervises onshore banks and can impose administrative penalties under Article 17. The FIU receives and analyses STRs. The EOCN oversees TFS and list notifications.

bank.question: A relationship manager argues that a customer cannot be a money launderer because he never committed the original fraud. What does Article 2 say?
options: Laundering requires taking part in the predicate offence, so he cannot be liable
Acquiring or using proceeds with the required knowledge is laundering
Laundering requires conviction of the fraudster first
Possession of proceeds is never an offence on its own
bank.explanation: Article 2(1)(c) includes acquiring, possessing or using proceeds on receipt, with knowledge or sufficient indications of their criminal origin. Participation in or conviction for the predicate offence is not required.

bank.question: The FIU orders a freeze on funds at Lumara suspected of being linked to a crime. Under Article 5, how long can that freeze last before extension?
options: Up to ten working days, with no extension
Indefinitely, until delisting
Up to thirty days, extendable by the Attorney General
Up to five business days, then automatic release
bank.explanation: Article 5(2) allows the head of the FIU to freeze suspected funds for up to thirty days, subject to extension by the Attorney General. The ten-working-day limit applies to suspending a transaction.

bank.question: Which description of the DIFC and ADGM is accurate for this quest's purposes?
options: Free zones with their own regulators and rulebooks
Districts where no AML law of any kind applies to licensed firms
Areas supervised directly by the UAE FIU
Branches of the CBUAE with identical rulebooks
bank.explanation: The DFSA regulates the DIFC and the FSRA regulates ADGM, each with its own rulebook. Onshore banks such as Lumara follow the CBUAE framework.

bank.question: A bank's representatives launder funds in the bank's name. What is the criminal fine range for the bank under Article 27(1)?
options: AED 5m to 100m, or the property's value if greater
AED 10,000 to AED 5 million for each violation found by the supervisor
AED 100,000 to 1 million
AED 50,000 minimum with no maximum
bank.explanation: Article 27(1) sets a fine of AED 5 million to 100 million, or the value of the criminal property involved, whichever is greater. AED 10,000 to 5 million is the supervisory administrative fine.

bank.question: Which statement about the National Committee is correct?
options: It files STRs on behalf of banks that lack a compliance officer
It licenses banks to operate onshore
It hears appeals against FIU freezes
It sets national strategy and assesses national risk
bank.explanation: Article 14 gives the National Committee competences including the national strategy, the national risk assessment and identifying high-risk countries. Banks file their own STRs with the FIU.

bank.question: Why did the 2025 reset matter for a bank's internal procedures?
options: Banks were exempted from CDD until new guidance appeared
New article numbers and duties replaced the 2018 law and 2019 decision
STRs moved from the FIU to the EOCN
The CBUAE stopped supervising AML
bank.explanation: Decree-Law No. 10 of 2025 replaced the 2018 law and Resolution 134 of 2025 replaced the 2019 decision. Duties continued without a gap, but procedures needed to map to the new texts.

bank.question: A corporate customer is owned 24% by Person A, 24% by Person B, who are unrelated and act independently, and 52% by a company listed on a securities market with adequate beneficial ownership disclosure. Which statement is correct?
options: Every shareholder of the listed company must be identified and verified
A and B must be recorded as beneficial owners because each owns more than 20%
Lumara need not identify the listed company's shareholders and may use public registers or other reliable sources
The account must be refused because no natural person owns 25%
bank.explanation: Article 11 allows a bank not to identify shareholders or beneficial owners of a listed company subject to adequate disclosure, using public registers or other reliable sources. A and B are each below the 25% test, and the absence of a 25% owner is not a reason to refuse.

bank.question: A trust is the customer. Which set of persons must Lumara identify under Article 10?
options: Settlor, trustee, protector, beneficiaries and any controller
Only the trustee who signs documents and operates the trust's bank account
Only beneficiaries who receive payments this year
Only the settlor, because they funded the trust
bank.explanation: Article 10(2) requires identifying the trustee, settlor, protector, beneficiaries or class of beneficiaries and any other natural person with ultimate effective control, including through chains.

bank.question: Which of the following is an example of enhanced due diligence named in Article 5?
options: Inferring the purpose of the relationship from the type of product and transaction used
Requiring the first payment from the customer's own account at an equivalent bank
Updating data at longer intervals
Verifying identity after the relationship starts
bank.explanation: Article 5(2)(c) lists EDD examples including the first payment through the customer's own account at an equivalently supervised institution. The other options are simplified measures.

bank.question: A low-risk customer's identity verification is deferred until after the account opens. Which condition does Article 6 impose?
options: Verification can wait until the first periodic review
Deferral is allowed for any customer who requests it
Verification must be completed as soon as possible and risks controlled meanwhile
Deferral needs FIU approval
bank.explanation: Article 6(2) allows deferral only for low risk, when necessary not to disrupt business, with verification completed as soon as possible and effective risk controls in place.

bank.question: A former foreign deputy minister who left office three years ago wants to open a private banking account. What is correct under Resolution 134?
options: He is no longer a PEP once he leaves office, so standard CDD is enough
He is a domestic PEP because he lives in Dubai
PEP rules apply only to serving officials' family members
He is still a PEP, so foreign PEP measures apply
bank.explanation: The definition covers persons who have previously been entrusted with prominent public functions. As a foreign PEP, Article 16(1)(a) measures apply, including senior approval and source of funds and wealth.

bank.question: Lumara's analyst finds a company's ownership chart cannot be verified and the customer refuses to explain a nominee shareholder. What is the correct action?
options: Open the account but flag it for review in a year
Do not establish the relationship and consider an STR
Open the account and apply simplified measures
Accept a signed undertaking from the nominee
bank.explanation: Where CDD measures cannot be applied, Article 14(1) prohibits establishing or continuing the relationship or executing transactions and requires the bank to consider an STR.

bank.question: Before opening a new correspondent relationship with a foreign bank, which step does Article 26 require?
options: Approval by the UAE FIU
Senior management approval after assessing the respondent
A deposit equal to the expected annual volume of payments through the account
A copy of every respondent customer's passport
bank.explanation: Article 26 requires information on the respondent's business, reputation and supervision, an assessment of its controls, senior management approval and clarity on each party's responsibilities. Shell banks are excluded.

bank.question: Which statement about simplified due diligence under Resolution 134 is correct?
options: It may be used whenever a customer is a UAE national with a salary account at a UAE bank
It removes the need to screen against sanctions lists
Allowed for identified low risk with the supervisor, keeping full TFS compliance
It applies automatically to all salary accounts
bank.explanation: Article 5(3) allows simplified measures where low risks are identified, in coordination with the supervisor, unless crime is suspected, and they must ensure full implementation of TFS instructions.

bank.question: A domestic PEP's relationship is rated high risk because of large unexplained transfers. Which measures now apply?
options: Only adequate measures to identify PEP status, because the person is a domestic PEP
Immediate account closure without review
Senior approval, source of funds and wealth checks, enhanced monitoring
Simplified due diligence because the PEP is domestic
bank.explanation: Article 16(1)(b) applies the foreign PEP measures in subparagraphs (2) to (4) to domestic and international organisation PEPs where the relationship is high risk.

bank.question: A customer tries to make a transfer, is asked about its purpose, and cancels it. Lumara has reasonable grounds to suspect the funds are criminal. Must an STR be considered even though no transaction completed?
options: No, only completed transactions are reportable
Only if the amount exceeds AED 55,000
Only if the customer is already under investigation
Yes, attempted transactions are covered by the reporting duty
bank.explanation: Article 18 of Resolution 134 applies to a transaction or attempted transaction, or funds, regardless of value. Abandoning a transaction when questioned can itself add to suspicion.

bank.question: The compliance officer reviews an internal report and decides not to file an STR. What must happen?
options: The employee who raised it is disciplined
The customer is told the review found nothing
The decision and its reasons are recorded and kept confidential
The report is deleted to protect privacy
bank.explanation: Article 22(2) requires the compliance officer to decide whether to notify the FIU or retain the matter, stating the reasons, in full confidentiality. Records are kept under Article 25.

bank.question: Lumara shares information about an STR with its majority-owned subsidiary's compliance team to manage group risk. Is this tipping off?
options: No, if done under group rules with confidentiality safeguards
Yes, any sharing outside the reporting branch is tipping off under Article 19
Yes, unless the FIU approves each disclosure in writing
No, and the subsidiary may tell the customer
bank.explanation: Article 19 of Resolution 134 preserves information sharing within the financial group under Article 32, which requires safeguards on confidentiality and against tipping off.

bank.question: A branch employee tells her cousin, who works at another company, that a mutual acquaintance's account has been reported to the FIU. Which provision is breached?
options: None, because the cousin is not the customer
Only the bank's social media policy
The record-keeping rule in Article 25
The tipping-off prohibition, which covers disclosure to any person
bank.explanation: Article 19 bars disclosure to the customer or any other person, directly or indirectly, and Article 29(1) of the decree-law punishes it. Disclosure to a third party is still tipping off.

bank.question: Why must records be organised so individual transactions can be reconstructed?
options: So the bank can market products to customers
So they can serve as evidence for prosecution where necessary
So customers can request deletion more easily
So the bank can avoid filing STRs
bank.explanation: Article 25(3) requires records to be organised to permit reconstruction of transactions, data analysis and tracing, so they can provide evidence for prosecution if needed.

bank.question: Which situation is a CDD threshold rather than a reporting threshold?
options: Any value for an STR
Suspicion regardless of amount
Any value for a sanctions match
AED 55,000 for occasional transactions
bank.explanation: AED 55,000 is the Article 7 trigger for CDD on occasional transactions. STRs and sanctions action apply regardless of value.

bank.question: Lumara receives an FIU request for more information on an STR it filed last month. What does Resolution 134 require?
options: Respond promptly, without relying on banking secrecy
Wait for a court order before replying
Ask the customer for permission first
Reply at the next annual review
bank.explanation: Article 18(1) requires prompt responses to FIU requests for additional information, and the duty applies without invoking banking or professional secrecy or contractual liability.

bank.question: An employee files an internal report about a customer in good faith. The customer later sues, claiming breach of confidentiality. What is the legal position?
options: The employee is personally liable because the customer's confidentiality was breached
The bank must settle because no crime was proven
Good-faith reporting is protected from liability under Article 37
Protection applies only to the compliance officer
bank.explanation: Article 37 covers financial institutions, board members, employees and representatives who furnish required information, even if unaware of the exact crime, unless the report was made in bad faith.

bank.question: An account was closed in 2024. CCTV footage of the customer at the branch was recorded in 2023. Absent any later event, until when must the footage be kept at least?
options: Until 2028, five years from recording
Until 2025, one year from closure
Until 2034, ten years from closure
Until 2029, five years from account closure
bank.explanation: Article 25(2) applies the five-year minimum to CCTV and ATM recordings along with CDD records, counted from the latest listed event, here account closure in 2024.

bank.question: A UN designation is published on a Friday evening. Lumara's branches are closed until Monday, but customers can use mobile banking all weekend. What does EOCN guidance expect?
options: Screening on Monday morning is enough, because branches are closed and staff are off
Screening only once the CBUAE issues a circular
Freezing only after a CNMR is acknowledged
Procedures that stop listed persons using funds over the weekend
bank.explanation: The guidance expects procedures for weekends and holidays so funds subject to freezing cannot be accessed. Only if no business or account access is possible may screening start at the first minute of business.

bank.question: A company is 30% owned by a designated person and 70% by non-designated persons with no links to him. Dividends are due to the designated person. What is correct?
options: Freeze the whole company because a designated person is a shareholder of record
Pay the dividends normally because the company is not frozen
Company not frozen; dividends due to him are frozen
Freeze 30% of every company account
bank.explanation: EOCN guidance treats 50% or less as a minority interest: the entity is not frozen, but funds due to the designated person must be frozen, and changes in ownership must be watched.

bank.question: Which parties does EOCN guidance say must be included in sanctions screening?
options: Customers, prospects, past customers, parties, owners and signatories
Only active customers with balances
Only new customers at onboarding
Only customers from high-risk countries and their immediate family members and associates
bank.explanation: The guidance lists existing customers, potential customers, previous customers up to five years, transaction parties, beneficial owners, connected persons, directors, agents and attorneys.

bank.question: After a freeze, a payment due under a contract signed before the designation arrives for the frozen account. What applies?
options: It must be returned to the sender
It may be paid out to the designated person
It requires a new CNMR before any action
It may be credited, but must be frozen immediately
bank.explanation: EOCN guidance allows additions to frozen accounts of interest and payments due under earlier contracts, provided they are immediately frozen.

bank.question: Screening shows a 40-year-old listed person shares a customer's name, but the customer is a 16-year-old student with matching ID. What should Lumara do?
options: Record it as a false positive with the reasons; no report is needed
File a PNMR as a precaution
Freeze the account until the EOCN responds
File a CNMR because the names match
bank.explanation: When key identifiers show the person is not the designated individual, the guidance treats it as a false positive: no report is required, but internal documentation must be kept.

bank.question: A trade client with no list matches requests an LC for goods that appear to be controlled dual-use items, shipped via a transhipment hub to an end user unrelated to the stated buyer. Which route is correct if suspicion remains after enquiries?
options: File an STR with the FIU through goAML
File a CNMR with the EOCN
File a PNMR with the EOCN
No report, because no names matched
bank.explanation: EOCN guidance says suspected sanctions evasion or PF without a confirmed or partial match on the UAE or UN lists is reported to the FIU as an STR or SAR. CNMRs and PNMRs are for list matches.

bank.question: Which three criteria does the EOCN apply when deciding permits for controlled dual-use goods?
options: Price, currency and payment terms
Technical specifications, end use and end user
Shipping line, insurer and port
Customer age, nationality and income
bank.explanation: The CPF guidance explains that EOCN permits rest on the item's technical specifications, its end use and its end user.

bank.question: A confirmed match concerns a prospect who has not yet opened an account. What must Lumara do?
options: Reject the business and file a CNMR within five business days
Open the account and then freeze it
File a PNMR because the prospect is not a customer
Decline without any report
bank.explanation: For a potential customer or counterparty with a confirmed match, the guidance requires rejecting the transaction or relationship, providing no funds or services, and filing a CNMR within five business days.

bank.question: Which state of affairs ends a TFS freeze on a confirmed match?
options: Delisting, or an EOCN cancellation via goAML
The expiry of thirty days, unless the Attorney General extends the freeze
A court judgment in the customer's home country
The customer proving the funds are lawful
bank.explanation: Under EOCN guidance, freezes have no time limit and end on delisting, unless another competent authority's freeze order applies, or on an EOCN cancellation decision via goAML.

bank.question: A CBUAE inspection finds that Lumara's policies were never approved by senior management. Which requirement is breached?
options: Article 25 on record keeping
Article 7 on CDD thresholds
Article 21 of Resolution 134 on internal policies
Article 28 of Resolution 134 on wire transfers and originator data
bank.explanation: Article 21 requires internal policies, controls and procedures approved by senior management and kept under ongoing review. The decree-law's Article 19 contains the same expectation.

bank.question: Which reporting line best protects the compliance officer's independence required by Article 22?
options: Reporting to the head of sales, who sets compliance targets
Management-level role with direct access to senior management and the board
Part-time role combined with branch management
Reporting only to an outsourced vendor
bank.explanation: Article 22 requires a management-level compliance officer with independence in decision-making, who reports directly to senior management. Placing the role under revenue-driven managers undermines that independence.

bank.question: Lumara's training records show completion rates but no tests and no role-based content. Which requirement is weakest?
options: Documented, ongoing capacity-building of relevant staff
The duty to report suspicion to the FIU without delay and regardless of value
The duty to register for EOCN alerts
The duty to keep CCTV recordings
bank.explanation: Articles 21(5) and 22(4) require periodic capacity-building programmes and documented ongoing training plans. EOCN guidance adds role-based PF and TFS training, so generic completion data alone is weak evidence.

bank.question: The CBUAE finds a director responsible for repeated AML failures. Which measure can it take under Article 17?
options: Sentence the director to prison
Confiscate the director's personal property
Deport the director without a court order
Suspend the director or request their replacement
bank.explanation: Article 17 lets the supervisor restrict powers of, suspend or request replacement of responsible directors and managers. Prison and confiscation require criminal proceedings before a court.

bank.question: Which audience does EOCN's CPF guidance single out for additional training on PF typologies and red flags?
options: Only staff in marketing
Only board members
Only branch security guards and reception staff in branches near the free zones
Compliance, audit and higher-risk business such as trade finance
bank.explanation: The CPF guidance expects all staff to learn PF basics, and staff in critical compliance and audit roles related to higher-risk products such as trade finance to receive additional typology training.

bank.question: After a CBUAE penalty, the supervisor orders Lumara to submit periodic reports on remediation. Which provision allows this?
options: Article 5 of Resolution 134
Article 17(2) of the 2025 decree-law
Article 21 of Cabinet Resolution 74 of 2020
Article 3 of the 2025 decree-law
bank.explanation: Article 17(2) allows the supervisor, when imposing administrative penalties, to require periodic reports on measures taken to remedy the violation.

bank.question: Which statement about publication of supervisory penalties is correct?
options: Penalties must always remain confidential
The supervisor may publish administrative penalties through media outlets
Only the FIU may publish penalties
Penalties are published only after a criminal conviction
bank.explanation: Article 17(4) allows the supervisory authority to publish the administrative penalties it imposes through various media.

bank.question: Lumara's group runs a subsidiary abroad. Which element must its group-wide programme include under Article 32?
options: A complete ban on sharing any customer information between group entities in different countries
CDD and risk information sharing with confidentiality safeguards
Separate STR filing by head office for every subsidiary transaction
Approval of subsidiary customers by the CBUAE
bank.explanation: Article 32 requires group-wide programmes covering information exchange for CDD and risk management, provision of information to group compliance and audit, and adequate confidentiality and anti-tipping-off safeguards.

bank.question: Which piece of evidence most directly shows a CBUAE inspector that senior management oversees AML/CFT/CPF?
options: A framed copy of the decree-law in the lobby
A marketing brochure on financial crime prepared for customers and published on the bank's website
Compliance officer reports recording management's decisions
Staff badges with a compliance slogan
bank.explanation: Article 22(3) periodic reports to senior management include their observations and decisions, and can be sent to the supervisor on request. They show oversight in action rather than on paper.
